rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The retention window will guide subsequent gradient trimming and selectivity tests.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient while holding the window and temperature fixed to test whether full resolution can be retained with a faster run.

Both runs achieved the maximum CRF, and the minimum resolution remains comfortably above 1.5. Halve the gradient duration again to seek a shorter fully resolved method while isolating the effect of gradient steepness.

The 4-minute gradient retains maximum CRF, but the first pair is near the resolution limit. Test higher temperature at the same gradient to assess whether faster elution and a selectivity shift can preserve full resolution.

Higher temperature worsened the critical first pair, so test 25 C to improve its selectivity while shortening the gradient to 2 minutes. Lowering phi1 slightly moderates gradient steepness; the last peak may elute during the final hold.

Narrow the gradient window by raising phi0 while retaining the strong final solvent and low temperature. The shallower slope may lift the first pair above R = 1.5 while keeping the last peak near the fast elution time of injection 5.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving the slope that achieved full resolution in injection 6. The stronger final solvent should accelerate the last peak, while this run tests whether the first pair remains sufficiently retained and resolved.
Raise phi0 one grid step to shorten late retention and make the gradient shallower. Check whether the first pair retains full resolution as it moves closer to the unretained region.
Increase temperature by one step to accelerate the last peak while testing the first pair’s resolution margin of 1.77. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate the temperature effect.

Test one higher starting organic fraction to seek a shorter fully resolved run at the maximum CRF already achieved. The first peak is near the unretained region, so this injection checks whether early-pair compression outweighs the benefit of a shallower gradient.

Return phi0 to 0.30 to avoid the early-peak compression seen at 0.35, and test one temperature step above the fastest fully resolved method. This brackets the temperature limit for preserving maximum CRF with the 2-minute gradient.

Reduce the gradient slope to try to recover full resolution of the first pair at 35 C. The last peak will likely elute later during the hold, but should remain comfortably within the 10-minute threshold for maximum CRF.

Lower phi0 to retain the first pair beyond the near-unretained region, where reducing the gradient slope alone had little effect. This tests whether stronger initial retention restores full resolution at 35 C while maintaining a short run.

Lower phi1 one step to make the gradient shallower and lift the critical first pair from R = 1.42 toward full resolution. The stronger initial retention established in injection 13 should make this pair more responsive to slope, while the last peak should remain well within 10 minutes.

Injection 14 is borderline despite its rounded CRF, and injection 9 remains the fastest clearly fully resolved method. Return to 25 C and slightly soften injection 7’s gradient to seek a larger resolution margin with all peaks still eluting in roughly 3 minutes.

Combine the starting fraction of injection 8 with the slightly gentler gradient endpoint of injection 15. This tests for a larger first-pair resolution margin while retaining maximum CRF and a last-peak time below 3 minutes.

Raise temperature one step from injection 16 to shorten retention while testing whether its gentler slope preserves more resolution margin than injection 9. The maximum CRF is already secured; this explores a nearby fully resolved alternative.

Test whether lowering temperature restores the early-pair resolution lost at phi0 = 0.35 and 30 C. This probes the high-phi0 boundary of the fastest gradient, while injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Back off the starting organic fraction to keep the first pair away from the unretained region. This intermediate-temperature variant of injection 15 should shorten retention while testing whether full resolution survives with a gentler gradient than injection 9.

Extend the local refinement around injection 16 by lowering phi1 one step to increase the first-pair resolution margin. This should preserve maximum CRF with a roughly 3-minute last-peak time; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test the intermediate temperature between injections 20 and 12, where the first-pair resolution crossed the acceptance threshold. This should shorten injection 20’s retention while preserving full resolution, although injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Lower phi0 one step from injection 21 to move the first pair farther from the unretained region while retaining a shallow gradient. Results at 25 and 35 C suggest this intermediate temperature can preserve maximum CRF with all peaks eluting in about 3 minutes.

Lower temperature one step from injection 22 to increase the critical first-pair resolution margin while keeping the first peak clearly retained. This tests a short, fully resolved alternative; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed method, and the maximum CRF is already secured.

Test a lower starting organic fraction while preserving the gradient slope of the fully resolved injection 7. This should keep the first pair farther from the unretained region and retain maximum CRF with a short run; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use the final injection for a gentler-slope refinement of injection 24, aiming to increase the first-pair resolution margin while retaining maximum CRF. Injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, with the last peak at 2.58 minutes.
